record.paper_title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree II: Overview and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Joint law of size-m clade counts
record.original_question: For each m, let N_m^(n) be the number of clades of size m in DTCS(n). Determine the joint distribution of the family (N_m^(n), 2 ≤ m ≤ n) well enough to compute covariances among clade counts and to derive central limit theorems for statistics built from these counts.

evidence.quote: The mean number of subclades of size m in DTCS(n) equals n/m a(n, m).
Open Problem 9 Write N(n)_m for the number of size-m clades in DTCS(n). Study the joint distribution of (N(n)_m , 2 ≤ m ≤ n) in such a way that one can calculate covariances and deduce CLTs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define the discrete-time critical beta-splitting tree DTCS(n) as the random rooted binary tree obtained by the following recursive construction. Start with the root labelled by the integer n. Whenever a node is labelled by an integer m ≥ 2, split it into two children labelled L and m − L, where L is an independent random variable on {1, 2, …, m − 1} with distribution

  P(L = i) = (1 / a(m)) · 1/(i (m − i)),  for i = 1, …, m − 1,

where a(m) = ∑_{i=1}^{m−1} 1/(i(m − i)) is the normalizing constant. Nodes labelled 1 are leaves. A clade of the tree is the set of leaves descended from any internal node, and the size of a clade is the integer label of that node. For each integer m with 2 ≤ m ≤ n, let N_m^{(n)} denote the number of clades of size m in DTCS(n).

It is known that E[N_m^{(n)}] = (n/m) · a(n, m) for an explicit kernel a(n, m). The problem is to determine the joint distribution of the random vector

  (N_m^{(n)} : 2 ≤ m ≤ n)

in sufficient detail to (i) compute the asymptotic covariances Cov(N_{m_1}^{(n)}, N_{m_2}^{(n)}) as n → ∞ for fixed or scaling indices m_1, m_2, and (ii) derive central limit theorems for linear (and more general) statistics built from the clade counts (N_m^{(n)}).
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (2024–2025) on the critical beta-splitting tree has established CLTs for heights of uniformly chosen leaves and joint convergence for height-related statistics, but the specific problem of determining the joint distribution of clade counts (N_m^{(n)}) with asymptotic covariances and CLTs for linear statistics does not appear to have been resolved in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: Some central limit theorems for critical beta-splitting trees
status_evidence.snippet: new joint central limit theorem for components of the height of a leaf chosen uniformly at random in the discrete version of a critical beta-splitting tree
status_evidence.claim: Recent CLT results focus on leaf heights, not clade counts N_m^{(n)}.

status_evidence.title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree II: Overview and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Open Problem 9: Write N(n)_m for the number of size-m clades in DTCS(n). Study the joint distribution of (N(n)_m, 2 ≤ m ≤ n) so that one can calculate covariances and deduce CLTs.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed as an open problem in the overview.

status_evidence.title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree III: The exchangeable partition representation and the fringe tree
status_evidence.snippet: exchangeable partition representation and the fringe tree
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work develops fringe-tree tools but does not announce a full solution of the joint clade-count distribution problem.
